events.title: NeXT Computer released
events.summary: NeXT shipped its first workstation on October 12, 1988 — a Motorola 68030 Unix box with Objective-C tooling and a magneto-optical drive.
events.about: NeXTSTEP bundled a Unix kernel, Display PostScript graphics, and Interface Builder for GUI apps. Tim Berners-Lee wrote the WorldWideWeb browser on a NeXT at CERN; id Software prototyped on NeXT; Apple acquired the company and its OS became macOS and iOS foundations. For web history, this is the machine the web was born on.

narrative.whyChosen: NeXT was the hardware platform where the web browser was invented and modern Apple OS lineage began.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved Unix workstations could ship with world-class developer tools and consumer-grade UI polish.
narrative.problemSolved: Higher-education and research labs needed powerful Unix machines with integrated object-oriented development environments.
